- 2026-08-31 [claude] The Delete key means two unrelated things in one product: on the Home Field it stashes the focused tile to the shelf (field_screen.rs:963), in the Files app it moves the selected file to the trash (actions.rs:87). The Files app even labels it "Delete · Trash" in its shortcut hint while the same key one surface away destroys no file at all. Worth a vocabulary decision rather than a blind fix — either the field's verb stops being Delete, or shelving and trashing are named as one reversible "put away".  `@legeos.papercut.the-delete-key-means-two-unrelated-things-in/1`

- 2026-08-26 [claude] The installed LegeOS set on the development machine was mixed-age: ten of thirteen packages more than a day older than lege-shell, so an Aug-25 shell was calling Session.Lifecycle1 and current lege_shell_v1 requests against an Aug-22 sessiond and an Aug-23 compositor. Every symptom is silent and reads as an application bug. scripts/reinstall-legeos-desktop.sh apparently did not rebuild everything, or was run with --skip-build; `lege doctor`'s new package-ages check now catches the state, but the script itself should be re-examined.  `@legeos.papercut.the-installed-legeos-set-on-the-development/1`

So the session tile's rung assignment and its click routing had no coverage at all, and the inverted rung rule (Shut down at the floor, Log out hidden) was invisible to the suite. Teaching the harness to carry WidgetSnapshots would let every widget's controls be tested where they are actually drawn.  `@legeos.papercut.the-home-field-s-own-reflow-focus-ops-tests-are/1`
- 2026-08-26 [claude] Every reported Home Field failure — slow/lossy typing, a dead shutdown button, no logout — was present in a tree where cargo test, clippy -D warnings and all seven xtask checks passed. The workspace gates cover model and layout arithmetic and cannot see the input thread, the rung a control lands on, or an interface that was never registered. Work that adds a user-facing surface should not be recorded as done on workspace evidence alone; the hands-on check needs to gate the commit, not trail it.  `@legeos.papercut.every-reported-home-field-failure-slow-lossy/1`
- 2026-08-25 [claude] `lege doctor` exited 1 on every developer install and made scripts/reinstall-legeos-desktop.sh refuse a perfectly good session. Two checks asked image-time questions at runtime: os-release demanded ID=legeos on an Ubuntu build host, and mime-handlers resolved handlers against LegeOS app manifests only, so all 156 real .desktop entries in the user's own KDE mimeapps.list read as missing. The 4KB single-line detail then buried both fail rows, so the operator saw only "do not log out until its failures are fixed" with no visible failure. Fixed: os-release skips at root "/", mime-handlers resolves against every XDG applications dir (snap and flatpak exports always included, not just what XDG_DATA_DIRS happens to carry), and the CLI abbreviates detail and prints a closing tally naming the failures.  `@legeos.papercut.lege-doctor-exited-1-on-every-developer-install/1`
